verdicts.question: Will BEE add a material-recovery or recycling methodology to the Indian Carbon Market offset mechanism (waste is a listed sector), and what floor and forbearance prices has CERC approved for carbon credit certificates? How many offset methodologies are approved today?
verdicts.problems: Verification could not be run: this session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200 of 200 calls) before this sceptic pass started and outbound page fetches are refused by the network policy, so not one of the 11 cited sources was re-found by a snippet and none of the figures could be confirmed as current on 30 September 2026. Default applied: holds=false. Beyond that, checks that could be done locally: (a) the '12 approved methodologies, last updated 7 July 2026' and the codes 'BM WA03.001/002/003' and 'BM-T-013' are not confirmed by any snippet and the repo's own carbon brief of 29 Sep 2026 (docs/plan/research/carbon.md) still says 8 methodologies per IETA 2025 while noting the ICM portal 'now lists 12' at indiancarbonmarket.gov.in/offset-mechanism/MzI=, a different URL from the beeindia.gov.in lid=571 page cited here, so the count and the page must be re-read; (b) the CERC CCC Regulations dates (notified 27 Feb 2026, gazette 3 Mar 2026), the 'monthly sessions on power exchanges' and 'floor and forbearance band approved by CERC on BEE's proposal' agree with the independent carbon brief in the repo, so they are consistent but still not snippet-confirmed; (c) the SWM Rules 2026 in-force date of 1 April 2026 agrees with the swm-2026 research file (gazette 28 Jan 2026, rule 1(2)); (d) the 'started on or after 1 January 2025' offset eligibility agrees with the carbon brief; (e) the analyst price guesses (Rs 400–1,200 and Rs 600–1,200/tCO2e) are correctly labelled unofficial, but no snippet confirms either range or the claim that CERC/BEE had approved nothing by 30 Sep 2026; because the compliance market's first monthly trading session is expected around October 2026, a BEE proposal and CERC approval of the price band in September 2026 is exactly the kind of newer development this pass could not check; (f) no arithmetic in the answer. Refined-chain gap: the decision records 'tonnes by material, source ward and destination' but a CDM-style recycling methodology (AMS-III.AJ, the likely template) credits recycled output at the pre-processor or recycler, not collection, so the methodology-ready data must also carry the material state (S0–S9), each processing record's main output, by-product and residual-waste lots and its yield, and the facility's energy use; without that the collection-level data alone would not support a claim.
verdicts.correction: Corrected answer (with the same caveat that no source could be re-opened in this pass): India's compliance carbon market (CCTS) has an offset mechanism whose Phase I sectors include waste handling and disposal, but as far as the repo's own research found (29 Sep 2026) none of the approved offset methodologies credits material recovery or recycling; the only waste methodologies deal with landfill methane, landfill-gas use and compressed biogas, plus a composting tool. The exact count (8 per IETA in 2025; 12 on the ICM portal per the researcher's read) and the methodology codes are unconfirmed and must be re-read on indiancarbonmarket.gov.in and beeindia.gov.in before any pitch. The CERC (Terms and Conditions for Purchase and Sale of Carbon Credit Certificates) Regulations, 2026 (notified 27 Feb 2026, gazetted 3 Mar 2026) provide for monthly trading on power exchanges within a floor and forbearance price band that CERC approves on BEE's proposal; whether rupee values have now been approved ahead of the first trading session expected around October 2026 could not be checked here and is an open item, so no floor or forbearance figure should be used; the Rs 400–1,200/tCO2e figures circulating are analyst estimates, not official. Offset projects must have started on or after 1 Jan 2025, so the 13 Oct 2026 pilot would qualify on timing if a recycling methodology ever appears; the SWM Rules 2026 (in force 1 Apr 2026) make segregation and recycling mandatory, which a regulatory-surplus test would have to reconcile. Decision stays: no CCTS revenue in the pilot model; but the methodology-ready ledger must record, per lot, material and state (S0–S9), source ward, destination, and for every pre-processor or recycler run the main output, by-product and residual lots with yield and facility energy, because any recycling methodology credits recycled output (S4–S7) rather than collection. Who to ask: BEE offset-mechanism cell (methodology plans and proposal route); CERC/BEE for the price band notification; re-check indiancarbonmarket.gov.in monthly.

verdicts.question: Can a tonne of plastic that generated a CPCB EPR certificate also earn a Verra plastic credit (WRC/WCC), given PWRM0001's additionality test? Is paper or cardboard creditable under any active methodology (VMR0007, GS 448)?
verdicts.problems: No source could be re-found by snippet (search budget exhausted, fetches refused), so the Verra 12 Aug 2024 clarification quote, the DTE 1 Sep 2026 figures and the CPCB documents are all 'not confirmed by snippet'. Substantive problems found locally: (1) The claim that VMR0007/AMS-III.AJ 'covers paper/cardboard' and 'credits avoided landfill methane where the baseline is decay in a dumpsite' contradicts the repo's own carbon brief (docs/plan/research/carbon.md, 29 Sep 2026), which lists the VMR0007/AMS-III.AJ eligible materials as HDPE, LDPE, PET, PVC, PP, container glass, aluminium and steel and states 'paper has no active VCS or GS carbon methodology found'; the materials research file likewise treats AMS-III.AJ as a virgin-material-displacement method with default factors for plastics, glass and metals (and AMS-III.BA for e-waste), not a methane-avoidance method. Until a snippet or the PDF shows paper in AMS-III.AJ's material list, paper must be treated as not creditable under VMR0007, which flips the second half of the answer. (2) The '30% discount to virgin-material displacement' figure has no corroboration anywhere in the repo (the brief says only 'a discount factor') and no snippet: unsourced number. (3) '17 million tonnes of certificates since 2022 against about 3.8 million tonnes a year' is not confirmed; the comparison is also cumulative-versus-annual (about 3.5 years, roughly 4.9 Mt a year on the researcher's own figures), which still exceeds generation but should be stated that way; CPCB's commonly cited generation figure is about 4.1 Mt (2020-21), so 3.8 Mt needs its source. (4) Items that are consistent with other repo research and general knowledge but still unconfirmed: certificates generated only by registered recyclers (PWPs) against GST e-invoices and sold to PIBOs (epr-portals research agrees); 2026-27 recycling targets 70/50/50 for categories I–III (matches PWM Amendment Rules 2022 Schedule II); AMS-III.AJ small-scale cap of 60,000 tCO2e/yr; GS 448 v1.0 (2 May 2025) scope 'metals, alloys and minerals' (materials research agrees); PWRM0001 non-additionality of EPR-covered material unless compliance is below 50% (carbon brief agrees). (5) The status 'answered' is too strong for an answer whose paper conclusion is disputed and whose key figures are unconfirmed; it should be 'partly'. Refined chain: the EPR certificate arises at the recycler (S5–S7 output, against the sale invoice), while a Verra WCC arises at collection (S1–S3) and a WRC at recycling output; the one-claim-per-lot rule must therefore follow the lot through state changes and yields, so a bale (S3) later flaked and certified (S7) cannot also carry a WCC for the same mass; residual-waste and by-product lots from a processing record are never creditable and must be split out.
verdicts.correction: Corrected answer: For the same tonne, no. Verra's PWRM0001 v1.1 additionality test (Step 1, regulatory surplus) requires every mandatory EPR scheme in the region to be listed, and the August 2024 clarification (as read by the researcher; not re-opened here) bars Waste Collection Credits for plastic already directly financed through an EPR scheme; PWRM0002 applies the same logic to recycling credits. In India the EPR certificate is generated on the CPCB portal by the registered recycler for each tonne recycled against a GST e-invoice of recycled-product sales and is sold or transferred to PIBOs, so a tonne that produced a certificate is EPR-financed and out. Collection of EPR-covered packaging plastic is treated as non-additional unless the scheme is shown 'not fully effective' (compliance or collection below 50% in the region) or the project exceeds the mandated threshold; with 2026-27 recycling targets of 70%/50%/50% for packaging categories I–III and CPCB certificate volumes reportedly exceeding annual generation (figure unconfirmed), a below-50% showing is unlikely for packaging; non-packaging plastics and tonnes the recycler does not certify remain candidates, subject to the VVB. Paper and cardboard: not eligible under Verra's Plastic Program (PWRM0001/0002 are plastic-only) and, on the evidence in this repo, not covered by VMR0007/AMS-III.AJ either, whose eligible materials are HDPE, LDPE, PET, PVC, PP, glass and metals; Gold Standard 448 covers only metals, alloys and minerals. So there is no active carbon or plastic methodology for paper recycling found; treat paper as 'track, don't credit' and confirm the AMS-III.AJ material list from the CDM PDF before saying otherwise. Chain mapping: EPR certificates attach at S5–S7 output at the recycler; WCCs at S1–S3 dispatch from kabadiwala or yard; WRCs at recycler output net of yield; residual-waste and by-product lots are excluded. Status: partly. Who to ask: a Verra-approved plastic VVB (SCS Global Services or Control Union) for a written view on Bengaluru's EPR effectiveness per material; CPCB EPR portal for regional compliance data; CDM AMS-III.AJ v9.0 text for the material list and factors.

verdicts.question: Should Luma.Green be the project proponent of a Verra grouped plastic project or partner with a developer such as Hasiru Dala Innovations or Plastics For Change? What does verification cost in India and how many tonnes a year does a plastic-credit project need to pay for itself? What revenue share do collector programmes (Plastic Bank, others) pay collectors, and will a verifier accept ward-level household location as evidence of source?
verdicts.problems: None of the 19 cited sources could be re-found by snippet in this pass (search budget exhausted before the pass began; fetches refused), so every figure is 'not confirmed by snippet'; default holds=false. Checks that could be done: (1) Arithmetic on the Verra fee example is internally correct given the stated tiers: 200 t = 100×1 + 100×3 + 500 annual = USD 900; 1,000 t = 100 + 1,200 + 2,500 + 500 = 4,300; 3,000 t = 100 + 1,200 + 2,500 + 10,500 + 5,000 + 500 = 19,800, i.e. USD 6.6/t; but the tier values themselves (USD 1/3/5/7/10 per credit; USD 5 per estimated annual tonne capped at 7,500) and the fee-schedule version 'v1.2 dated 30 Mar 2023 at a 2024/02 URL' are unconfirmed, and the one-off registration fee is left out of the per-year figures. (2) The source title says Verra's five-year note reports '500,000+ credits' while the repo's carbon brief of 29 Sep 2026 says 'about 40,000 credits across 40+ projects'; one of these is wrong by an order of magnitude and neither could be checked; the '36 registered projects in 20 countries' figure is likewise unconfirmed. (3) 'India listings limited to' three 2022 projects is a currency claim about the Verra registry in 2026 that no snippet supports; newer Indian listings since 2022 are likely and this should be re-checked on registry.verra.org. (4) Collector-payment figures conflict internally (USD 0.16/kg bonus per The Walrus versus USD 0.01/kg per Plastic Bank's help centre) and neither is confirmed; the rePurpose USD 0.50/kg (2022) figure is four years old. (5) The Plastic Standard 'v1.0 (10 Feb 2021)' agrees with the repo's sources list, but whether Verra has since issued a newer Plastic Standard or Program Guide version could not be checked. (6) The '~1,000 t/yr of non-EPR-financed plastic' threshold in the decision is a judgement, not a sourced number, and should be labelled as such. Refined chain: the answer treats kabadiwalas and Saathis as the grouped-project instances, which is right for PWRM0001 collection (S1–S3), but PWRM0002 recycling credits attach at the pre-processor or recycler (S4–S7 output, net of yield, excluding residual-waste lots), so the partner choice and the evidence pack must name which state the credit is claimed at; ward-level household location is evidence for the S0→S1 source only, while everything from S2 onward needs site GPS, weigh slips, invoices and GRNs per processing record.
verdicts.correction: Corrected answer: Partner rather than be proponent in the pilot; the reasoning stands but the numbers are unverified. Verra's Plastic Waste Reduction Standard v1.0 (10 Feb 2021; check for a newer version) allows a grouped project with a designated geographic area, instances added at each verification against pre-set eligibility criteria and ownership evidence from each instance's start date, a 7-year crediting period renewable twice or 10 years fixed, and verification at least every three years, with validation possible alongside first verification. Being proponent means carrying the additionality file (EPR-covered packaging is probably non-additional in Bengaluru, see Q2) and the VVB audit bill. Verra's own fees are small compared with credit prices (the researcher's reading of the Plastic Program fee schedule gives roughly USD 900/yr at 200 t, USD 4,300/yr at 1,000 t and USD 19,800/yr at 3,000 t, under USD 7 per tonne, plus a one-off registration fee; tiers unconfirmed), but the real gate is the VVB validation/verification quote and MRV staffing, which no public page states for India, so the break-even tonnage cannot be given: tonnes × (net credit price − collector premium) must exceed VVB + MRV + Verra fees, and the missing input is a written VVB quote. Registry facts to re-check before use: the number of registered plastic projects and credits issued (the cited note and the repo brief disagree: 500,000+ versus about 40,000) and which Indian projects are listed today. Collector economics: Plastic Bank pays local market rate plus a bonus (public figures range from USD 0.01/kg to USD 0.16/kg and are unconfirmed); rePurpose Global does not publish the worker share; Plastics For Change offers a guaranteed minimum price plus a community premium with no published percentage; so the collector premium is an open item to settle with the partner. Evidence of source: PWRM0001 needs identifiable sources, dry weights at dispatch cross-checked with invoices and GRNs, and the Plastic Standard accepts one geodetic coordinate plus enough geographic information per site for sampling; ward-level household location plus kabadiwala shop GPS, weigh slips and invoices is the expected package for the S0→S1 step, with the VVB's sampling visit deciding. Chain mapping: WCC instances are kabadiwalas and yards (S1–S3); WRC instances are pre-processors and recyclers, credited on S4–S7 output per processing record net of yield, with residual-waste and by-product lots excluded; each lot carries one claim status across EPR certificate, WCC, WRC and carbon. Status: partly (or needs-pilot-or-counsel for the break-even). Who to ask: SCS Global Services and Control Union for quotes; rePurpose/Saahas and Plastics For Change/HDI for partner terms and the actual per-kg premium; Verra registry for current Indian project and credit counts.
